findings.title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting defeats the $__range guard
findings.body: Queries are now passed through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() on line 299 before partition() calls querySupportsSplitting() on line 300. querySupportsSplitting() (lines 282-289) relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) still seeing the literal $__range / $__range_s / $__range_ms variable, with the comment explaining such queries must not be split because the variable must be evaluated against the full, unsplit range. Once applyTemplateVariables expands that variable using the original request's range/scopedVars, the check can no longer detect it, so a query such as count_over_time({a="b"}[$__range]) is treated as splittable and is executed once per daily chunk, each chunk incorrectly using the full-range duration instead of being sent as a single unsplit request. This silently changes query semantics and results for $__range queries.

findings.title: Shard-split queries are interpolated twice, including ad-hoc filter application
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() now interpolates every target with datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) on line 52, but the resulting targets are later passed to runSplitQuery() (shardQuerySplitting.ts line 163), which after this PR interpolates every target again with the same scopedVars and filters (querySplitting.ts line 299). Template interpolation is not guaranteed idempotent: applyTemplateVariables also applies ad-hoc filters to the expression, so shard-split queries with ad-hoc filters get the same label matcher/filter appended twice, and variable values introduced by the first expansion that contain $-patterns can be expanded again on the second pass. The updated test even codifies this by expecting applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times for one original target. Shard splitting should either skip the second interpolation or not pass filters/re-interpolate already-interpolated targets, otherwise shard queries can produce duplicated or corrupted LogQL compared with the non-shard path.
